analysis.title: How Low Can You Go
key_insights: The S&P 500 is printing a year-low in P/E valuation, per FactSet.
The S&P 500 P/E relative to profitability has fallen to its lowest level in almost 14 years, per Bloomberg.
France is at lows in both bonds and equities: French equity valuations are closing in on a 10-year low, per BofA Quant. One chart plots France relative performance against OAT-Bund yield spreads.
NYSE available cash as a percentage of market capitalization has fallen to its lowest level on record, per @i3_invest.
S&P Top 50 real correlation has fallen to a new all-time low, per Barclays.
Average correlations among the most diversified sector combinations have also reached historic lows, per Barclays.
Token prices are declining on the back of high competition at the AI model layer, per BofA / Ramp.
Google's capital expenditures are at a record, and the note asks when that spending will show up in revenues, per Bloomberg.
Britain's rolling ten-year real household disposable income growth is at historic lows, per OBR.
CTAs have been aggressively selling into recent lows, particularly in tech, per GS.

Record Google capex with no clear timing for when it shows up in revenues.
Falling AI model token prices from competition at the model layer.

tension_points.bull_case: S&P 500 P/E is at a year-low and P/E relative to profitability is at a 14-year low, so valuations look cheap against earnings quality.
